controls.label: Thermal glow
controls.qualification: Black-body color at its measured dayside temperature, 2,346 K. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of WASP-19 b's heat: a black body at the dayside brightness temperature measured in secondary eclipse at 3.6 µm (Spitzer Space Telescope satellite Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)). Its star lights the day side; the night side is not measured. Reflected starlight is not included.

controls.label: Spitzer
controls.qualification: Published fit · Bell et al. (2021) · a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 80073, first published by Wong et al. (2016)) · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature at 4.5 µm of WASP-19 b from Bell et al. (2021)'s published fit to a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve (program 80073, first published by Wong et al. (2016)). Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 25° west of noon. The false color runs from 950 to 2,500 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of Wattle's planets in this map from above, to scale, with WASP-19 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

WASP-19 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 9 measured bins from Bean et al. 2013 (Magellan II Landon Clay Telescope, MMIRS), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors. The archive holds 1 other paper for this planet; this chart draws the one with the most bins.

WASP-19 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (89, 90, 99) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 35516889, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 6-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
